newsitem.title: CHINA: China PICC reinsurance sees 100 mln yuan business.
newsitem.headline: China PICC reinsurance sees 100 mln yuan business.

text.p: China's PICC Reinsurance Co hopes to take in 100 million yuan ($12 million) in commercial reinsurance business this year from domestic insurers this year, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
About $400 million in foreign currency insurance premiums leaves China each in a market dominated by foreign competitors, the newspaper said.

China's insurance firms prefer to export premiums even though they are required by law to give priority to domestic insurers when selling reinsurance, the newspaper quoted an official of PICC Reinsurance as saying.
PICC Reinsurance's business expansion is also hampered by its own position as a state reinsurer and subsidy of the state People's Insurance Company (Group) of China.

Under China's insurance law, domestic insurers must distribute 20 percent of the business to PICC Reinsurance to diversify risk and after handing over this compulsory business most insurers are reluctant to give commercial opportunities to PICC Reinsurance, the newspaper said.
Foreign firms also provide overseas training and travel opportunities, which act as added attractions.
Reinsurance provides a short-cut to foreign insurers to reach China's potentially huge insurance market since so far only four foreign insurers have operating licences in China, the newspaper said.

"Compared to the long wait for business licences in China, the Chinese reinsurance business requires less investment but brings quick gains," the newspaper quoted the PICC Reinsurance official as saying.
"The reinsurance business in an underdeveloped market is highly profitable," she said.
The official said the export of premiums had resulted in outflows of foreign exchange that was needed in China.
Foreign insurers have estimated that 20-30 percent of total foreign exchange premiums were leaving China, a number that was continuing to grow.
